newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador offers tender details for telecom sale.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador offers tender details for telecom sale.

text.p: The government of Ecuador on Monday took the first step in the privatization of 35 percent of Emetel by offering tender specifications for the sale, scheduled for September, a government official said on Monday.

An official at the National Council of Modernization, the agency in charge of privatizations, said interested companies could buy the prospectus for the state-owned telecommunications concern for $30,000.
The specifications provide details on Andinatel SA and Pacifictel SA, the two operating companies to be formed through the division of Emetel ahead of the sale.

"Through this operation, Ecuador is giving away concessions for the exploitation of the telecommunications market for 15 years, of which the first five years will be exclusive," a statement from the Council said.
The Emetel privatization was initially scheduled for April but the removal of former President Abdala Bucaram in February led to the sale's postponement.

In November, when Bucaram's government initially launched the sale, MCI Communications Inc and GTE Corp of the United States, Italy's Stet SpA, Telefonica de Espana SA and Korea Telecom presented the documentation to take part in the privatization.
The government will maintain 55 percent of the telecommunications company and 10 percent will be offered to employees.
The 35 percent to be sold to investors will represent a controlling stake.
